text.p: Smith Barney said on Friday it raised its recommendation for Mexican telephone company Telefonos de Mexico to outperform from neutral.
-- "Local revenue growth should be strong. Economic recovery should bring positive surprises in volume and line growth," analyst Peter Treadway said in a report.
-- Treadway said the company's cellular and local service are "two jewels in the crown." He estimated local revenues will grow in real terms by 15 percent in 1997 and 23 percent in 1998.
-- Long distance damage from entering competition should be quelled by expected economic growth and subsequently higher overall calling volume, he added.
-- Over the next five years Treadway estimated earnings growth of 12 percent. A reduction in the workforce, which could be announced in 1998, would further enhance the stock, he added.
-- The company's Mexican shares opened up 0.20 peso to 20.40 pesos from Thursday's close. The American Depositary Receipts rose 0/14 to 52/11 in early trading.
